2026-10-27.text:
Only one forecast calls for a southerly day in Squamish (it happens to be the one that works better on this area, but none of the others aligned). Environment Canada has Howe Sound southerly 10 to 20 near noon, and the outflow is gone: Pam Rocks reads N 2 at 7am and Pemberton is a touch below Vancouver.

My best guess today is the Nexen from noon to about 4pm, SSW 13 to 14 gusting 17. Low tide is 11ft at 1pm. It’s grey all day, so don’t expect extra thermal. If the Spit vane is south and reading 10+ by 11am, drive up.

English Bay buoy reads W 10 gusting 12, ahead of the page’s 6. If it hits 12+ by 10am, Jericho could be a foil option.

2026-10-26.text:
The outflow is on its way out. Pam Rocks read N 21 at 7am, down from 30 at 2am but still ahead of the page’s 18. Pemberton is still 4 hPa above Vancouver, which usually keeps it blowing a few more hours.

Porteau is a maybe until about 10am, on the ebb from 14.9ft. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go. Under 20, stay home.

2026-10-25.text:
Proper outflow Sunday. Pam Rocks reads NNE 21 at 5am, still a touch behind the page’s 27 to 28, and Environment Canada calls it stronger again.

My pick is Porteau from first light around 7:20 until about noon, NNE 22 to 28 with good swell. The tide drops from 14.2ft at 6am to 9.2ft at 11:30, then the flood starts, so go early. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go.

Backup is Boundary Bay, E 14 to 18 until about 9:30am, then about 13 from 1:30pm to last light, once the tide is back over 10ft.

2026-10-24.text:
Easterly Saturday. Sand Heads already reads E 14 at 5am and Point Atkinson ESE 11, a few knots ahead of the page, and Environment Canada calls 15 to 20 this afternoon.

I think we may run out of light, but Boundary Bay from about 1:30pm is a possibility. The page shows ENE 9 to 11, and the tide peaks at 13.2ft at 4:30pm, so plenty of water.

At Porteau, Pam Rocks forecast reaches 21, which is usually short of what it needs to fire up Porteau, but worth monitoring. Erwin Park usually works on an easterly, so worth monitoring too, but the forecast on this site disagrees today.

Tomorrow looks like a strong Porteau outflow: 28 at 10am, 84%.

2026-10-23.text:
The northwest is easing faster than I hoped. The Ferry Terminal dropped from 15 at 6am to 11 at 8am, and the tide is now too low on the south side until about 11:30am. I’m calling Tsawwassen off.

The only maybe is Porteau. Pam Rocks is building from the north, 12 at 8am, and the tide bottoms at 7.5ft around 10am. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ before 10am, go. Otherwise it fades by late morning.

Skipping Squamish: the valley is 6°C colder than Pam Rocks and Pemberton is still 2 hPa above Vancouver.

2026-10-22.text:
Northwest day, and Environment Canada has a gale coming: NW 15 to 25 this morning, 25 to 35 by early evening. Halibut Bank already reads W 11 gusting 13 at 5am, a little ahead of the page.

Jericho is my pick from about noon to 6pm with waves building late.  Ferry Terminal should also be about the same if you would want to sail in flat water. If the buoy reads 12+ from the west by 1pm, go.

2026-10-21.text:
Quiet Wednesday. The Howe Sound outflow is back and a bit stronger than the page shows: Pam Rocks was NNW 19 gusting 28 at 4am and 17 gusting 24 at 5am. Porteau is the only maybe. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north before 9am, go early while the tide is low (6.4ft at 8:15am). The flood after that can flatten the swell.

I’m skipping Squamish. The valley is 7°C colder than Pam Rocks, Pemberton is 4 hPa above Vancouver, and clouds are coming.

Thursday looks like the day: Jericho W 15 to 20 from noon, high tide 14ft at 3:50pm.

2026-10-20.text:
The northwest is blowing a bit more than the page shows: the English Bay buoy had W 12 gusting 18 at 8am. Jericho could work until about noon, WNW 12 to 15. If the buoy still reads 12+ from the west after 1pm, the afternoon is on too, with a 14ft high tide at 2:52pm.

Tsawwassen’s north side works on NNW once the tide passes 10ft, around 11:30am if you are foiling

Porteau is fading (Pam Rocks 17 at 7am, needs 22). Howe Sound outflow is back tonight, so Porteau could be on early Wednesday.
